rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a poor-quality early blastocyst and absent/indistinct ICM, but it overstates certainty about degenerative TE/debris and calls it a Day 4 blastocyst despite the image/lab grade being more consistent with an early blastocyst-level assessment rather than a clearly organized blastocyst.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, endometrium, first-cycle status, and semen data well, and appropriately concludes that embryo quality is the dominant limiting factor; only minor overinterpretation of the male-factor discrepancy.

Reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with conclusions broadly supported by the morphology and patient context; minor issues include some overconfident statements about nonviability and developmental lag from a single static image.

Largely aligned with Gardner-style grading interpretation and evidence-based IVF counseling, including caution against unproven add-ons and not rushing to PGT-A in a first cycle at age 32; slight deviation in treating the 0D label as strongly definitive from one image.

Provides practical next steps for transfer counseling, luteal support, lifestyle optimization, semen/fertilization review, and future culture strategy; recommendations are useful though somewhat generic in places.
